blocks.text: Heritage Woods home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

23 houses sold in Heritage Woods with a median price of $2,098,000 (the middle half sold between $1,872,500 and $2,265,000), taking a median of 18 days to sell at 96.8% of the last list price; 9% sold above list. They had a median $558 per square foot, a median year built of 2004 and a median lot of 6,515 square feet. 21 townhomes sold in Heritage Woods with a median price of $1,158,000 (the middle half sold between $997,000 and $1,280,000), taking a median of 16 days to sell at 98.3% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $631 per square foot, a median year built of 2004 and a median strata fee of $469 a month.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Heritage Woods PM

Filing position — stated openly at the top. Heritage Woods is a board (MLS) sub-area of the City of Port Moody — the eastern part of the Heritage Mountain grouping on the city's north shore. Port Moody's current Official Community Plan is OCP Bylaw 2026, No. 3522 (adopted April 28, 2026, repealing Bylaw No. Name trap flagged at the top: a "Heritage Woods Senior Living" website exists online, but it is generic non-BC content with no Port Moody address and no Assisted Living Registry registration — it is excluded with its reason in and is not a building in this area.
Streets, schools and getting around Heritage Woods PM

items.t: Heritage Woods is a hillside neighbourhood on Port Moody's north shore, the eastern part of the Heritage Mountain grouping in the Official Community Plan, below Anmore and beside the Coquitlam border, at the eastern end of the grouping. Boundary roads are UNVERIFIED from the OCP map. David Avenue connects Heritage Woods west into Port Moody and east into Coquitlam; Heritage Mountain Boulevard connects south toward Ioco Road.
Where condo stock concentrates: there is no apartment-condo shelf to concentrate. — listing counts as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.

SnapStats publishes listings, solds and ratios at sub-area level; medians are community level only. Port Moody IS SnapStats-covered, cited only as the reports state — there is no Heritage Woods median. SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.

Schools: Heritage Woods Secondary School at 1300 David Avenue is the area's landmark public building (SD43); an SD43 School Locator run for that address returned Heritage Mountain Elementary, Eagle Mountain Middle and Heritage Woods Secondary. Catchments are address-based — confirm any specific address in the locator.

Parks, recreation and transit: Bert Flinn Park, the large forested park on the north shore, borders the Heritage Mountain grouping neighbourhoods; Heritage Mountain Community Centre is at 200 Panorama Place and Port Moody Public Library at 100 Newport Drive. TransLink buses serve the north shore and connect to Moody Centre Station and Coquitlam Central Station; specific route numbers serving Heritage Woods are UNVERIFIED.
Health: Eagle Ridge Hospital is in Port Moody at 475 Guildford Way (Fraser Health) — down the hill from this sub-area, inside the same city.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Heritage Woods PM

items.t: Creek and slope rules that bite on this hillside: lots with a watercourse need a riparian assessment and Zoning Bylaw Section 5.4 setbacks, and environmentally sensitive and steep slope development permit areas can apply. No floodplain or ALR land was confirmed in Heritage Woods.

Port Moody property taxes: for 2026, due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on outstanding amounts after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 15, 2026; utilities are billed separately, with the 2026 utility bill due February 27, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about Heritage Woods PM

items.t: Detached demand led Port Moody here in September 2026 — attached did not. SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.

The OCP protects this hillside's character on paper. Chapter 14, Section 14.3 policies for the Heritage Mountain grouping aim to retain the existing residential and forested character — a reason no seniors tower or care campus is planned for this sub-area in the OCP (now Bylaw 2026, No. 3522).

Port Moody's seniors-housing action is all happening down the hill. Council declined a Kyle Seniors Housing proposal at second reading on Oct 14, 2025 (5-1), then directed staff to investigate affordable seniors housing opportunities — all Moody Centre items, with nothing proposed for Heritage Woods.

Kyle Centre, the older-adult hub serving the city, is being replaced. The 1977 Kyle Centre at 125 Kyle Street is at end of life; its redevelopment's first phase — conceptual design for a proposed 39,000 sq ft facility, plaza and expanded Kyle Park — began in summer 2025, funded with $515,000 from the Community Amenity Contribution Reserve, with room kept for potential future affordable housing at the west end of the City-owned lands under a separate project.
Cobalt Sky's published facts disagree with each other. Neither figure should be quoted in a listing — the strata plan BCS2068 and the Form B are the settlement documents.

Both commute doors matter on this hillside. David Avenue runs east into Coquitlam as well as west into Port Moody, so Heritage Woods buyers working in either direction use the neighbourhood differently — and neither route involves a SkyTrain station in the sub-area itself.

A single house listing here was flagged "Senior Community: No." MLS data carried in a current Heritage Woods rental listing (119 Aspenwood Dr) explicitly records "Senior Community, No" for the property — a small, concrete example of the sub-area's non-seniors character in the board's own data.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Heritage Woods PM

items.t: Form B diligence (every counted strata): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

City zoning and SSMUH: Zoning Bylaw No. 2937 puts single-detached homes in RS zones and multi-residential homes in RT and RM zones; small-scale multi-unit housing, including coach houses and accessory dwelling units, is permitted in RS and RT zones outside the transit-oriented areas. Hillside diligence: lots with a watercourse need a riparian assessment and Zoning Bylaw Section 5.4 setbacks, and environmentally sensitive and steep-slope development permit areas can apply. No floodplain or ALR land was confirmed in Heritage Woods.

Port Moody property taxes: 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on outstanding amounts after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 15, 2026; utilities are billed separately (2026 utility bill due February 27, 2026). This staged 5% + 5% is Port Moody's own municipal scheme as the City publishes it — it is not the Mission flat-10% regime and not the rural Taxation (Rural Area) Act regime.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Heritage Woods?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 18 houses and 6 condos and townhomes listed in Heritage Woods. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: Is Heritage Woods a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In September 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 22% (a sellers’ market). The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. One month in one community is a small sample, so look at the monthly table above before you decide.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Heritage Woods from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 11 houses and 4 condos and townhomes sold in Heritage Woods over those 4 months; detached houses peaked in September with 4 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in June with 3 sold.

faq.q: How big is Heritage Woods compared with the rest of Port Moody?
faq.a: In September 2026, Heritage Woods held 13.3% of the 135 detached houses listed in Port Moody and 3.1% of the 192 condos and townhomes listed in Port Moody.

faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in Heritage Woods?
faq.a: In September 2026, houses made up 75.0% of the 24 homes listed in Heritage Woods and condos and townhomes made up 25.0%; of the 4 that sold, houses were 100.0% and condos and townhomes 0.0%.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Heritage Woods than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses fell from 20 in June to 18 in September 2026 (−10.0%); condos and townhomes rose from 3 in June to 6 in September 2026 (+100.0%).

faq.q: What did houses in Heritage Woods sell for?
faq.a: 23 houses sold in Heritage Woods between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $2,098,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Heritage Woods?
faq.a: The median was 18 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 96.8% of the last list price (9% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: Is there an apartment condo I can buy in Heritage Woods?
faq.a: No verified one. A buyer set on an apartment here is, in practice, shopping Port Moody's apartment stock down the hill (Moody Centre / Inlet Centre), not in Heritage Woods.

faq.q: How did Heritage Woods sell in September 2026?
Is there a Heritage Woods retirement residence?
faq.a: No. A website called "Heritage Woods Senior Living" publishes generic content with no Port Moody address; BC's Assisted Living Registry and the Zone 4 directory list no such residence here, and the 55+ program found zero 55+ stock of any kind in the sub-area.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Heritage Woods townhome?
faq.a: Long-term, yes — rental-restriction bylaws are void province-wide since November 24, 2022, including the restriction element still printed in Cobalt Sky's building profile. A strata can still restrict short-term rentals by bylaw.
